title: AI-Powered Tools for Enhancing Writing Skills of English Language Learners: A Systematic Literature Review
venue: International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science (IJRISS)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the growing use of artificial intelligence tools to support English writing among English as a Second Language (ESL) and English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners. The review asks two main questions: which AI tools have been used to enhance writing skills, and how these tools improve different dimensions of writing. The authors argue that rapid AI development, especially since 2023, has outpaced earlier reviews and created a need for an updated synthesis.

Using PRISMA 2020 procedures, the authors systematically reviewed 31 studies published between 2021 and 2025 from ERIC and Web of Science. The included studies covered a range of methodologies and focused mainly on AI-powered writing tools such as ChatGPT, Grammarly, QuillBot, Gemini, and other automated writing evaluation or feedback systems. The synthesis examined outcomes across grammar and mechanics, vocabulary and style, feedback and revision, and narrative writing.

The reviewed evidence largely concerns student populations in ESL/EFL contexts, with a strong skew toward tertiary education and limited representation from primary and secondary settings. The paper notes that the included studies span varied sample sizes and designs, including mixed-methods, quasi-experimental, experimental, qualitative, and case studies. The review is not confined to one country; it synthesizes studies from multiple contexts, though a single study-country for the review itself is not specified beyond the authors’ institutional affiliation in Malaysia.

The main conclusion is that AI tools generally function as effective writing supports, especially for feedback and revision, grammar accuracy, and vocabulary development. ChatGPT was the most frequently studied tool, followed by Grammarly, QuillBot, and Gemini. The authors conclude that AI tools can improve ESL/EFL learners’ writing quality, but they also caution that AI should supplement rather than replace teachers, and that more longitudinal and non-tertiary research is needed to determine whether gains persist after the tools are removed.

identified_tools.name: AI-powered writing tools
identified_tools.description: A heterogeneous category of AI-supported writing assistance technologies, including automated writing evaluation systems, grammar and style checkers, paraphrasing tools, and generative AI writing assistants that provide feedback or revision support for written text.
identified_tools.use_case: Systematic review of 31 studies (2021-2025) examining how AI-supported writing tools were used in ESL/EFL writing instruction, predominantly in tertiary education.

findings.finding_summary: Across 31 reviewed studies, AI-powered writing tools were synthesized as useful supports for ESL/EFL writing, with reported benefits including immediate feedback, fewer grammatical errors, broader lexical variety, and stronger revision support. No pooled effect size was reported.
findings.measure: ESL/EFL writing performance and writing skill development across reviewed studies

findings.finding_summary: Eight reviewed articles indicated that AI grammar checkers and automated writing evaluation tools improved grammar and mechanics by identifying and correcting grammar, spelling, and punctuation errors. Immediate feedback was described as helping learners recognize and fix errors in real time.
findings.measure: grammar, spelling, punctuation, and writing accuracy

findings.finding_summary: Seven reviewed articles suggested that AI tools improved vocabulary and style by offering alternative words and phrases, supporting more varied lexical choices and clearer expression.
findings.measure: vocabulary diversity, style, expressiveness, and fluency

findings.finding_summary: Feedback and revision was the strongest area of support: 24 of 31 included articles reported that AI tools helped learners improve writing through feedback and subsequent revision, often highlighting instant feedback, self-paced learning, and learner autonomy.
findings.measure: feedback use, revision processes, and improvement through written corrective feedback

findings.finding_summary: Two reviewed articles reported potential for AI tools to improve narrative writing, including more expressive narrative styles and creative elements.
findings.measure: narrative writing skill and creativity in narrative style

findings.finding_summary: The review reports that AI tools may foster learner autonomy through instant feedback and self-paced learning, while also raising concerns about overdependence on AI and the need for teacher guidance so that AI supplements rather than replaces learners' own writing development.
findings.measure: learner autonomy, dependence on AI, and responsible AI use in writing

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: Generative AI chatbot that produces and revises natural-language text, answers prompts, and provides writing support through conversational interaction.
identified_tools.use_case: This review identifies ChatGPT as the most frequently used AI tool for improving ESL/EFL writing skills, appearing in 16 of the 31 included studies (Alshammari, 2024; Chan et al., 2024; Cheng, 2024; Ghafouri et al., 2024; Karataş et al., 2024; Long, 2024; Mahapatra, 2024; Moussa & Belhiah, 2024; Özdere, 2025; Polakova & Ivenz, 2024; Seo, 2024; Shen et al., 2023; Solovey, 2024; Song & Song, 2023; Yu-Ching & Lin, 2024; Zaiarna et al., 2024). The review says it was valued for idea organization, essay structuring, personalized feedback, iterative dialogue, vocabulary support, feedback/revision support, and narrative writing assistance.

findings.finding_summary: The review reports that ChatGPT was the most prevalent tool and was consistently described as improving overall writing quality through immediate support for idea organization, essay structuring, and personalized feedback.
The review states that ChatGPT helped diversify vocabulary and improve expressiveness and fluency by offering personalized vocabulary suggestions and alternative phrasing.

The review reports that ChatGPT played a major role in feedback and revision processes, with studies describing instant critiques, self-paced revision, and improved essay quality, participation, and motivation when AI-generated feedback was used.
The review notes that ChatGPT showed potential for developing narrative writing skills by helping students overcome writer's block and explore expressive narrative styles.

identified_tools.name: Grammarly
identified_tools.description: AI writing assistant that checks grammar, spelling, punctuation, clarity, and style and provides revision suggestions for written text.
identified_tools.use_case: The review identifies Grammarly in seven studies (Dizon & Gayed, 2021; ElEbyary et al., 2024; Lee et al., 2024; Nurul et al., 2022; Sanosi, 2022; Thangthong et al., 2024; Wei et al., 2023). It is discussed as a prominent AWE tool that provides real-time written corrective feedback on grammar, clarity, and conciseness, mainly supporting grammar/mechanics and revision.

findings.finding_summary: The review reports that Grammarly significantly reduced grammatical errors and supported real-time correction of grammar, spelling, and punctuation, improving surface-level writing accuracy.
The review states that Grammarly increased lexical variety, though its benefits were characterized mainly as surface-level rather than higher-order writing improvement.

identified_tools.name: QuillBot
identified_tools.description: AI writing and paraphrasing assistant that rewrites text, suggests alternative phrasing, and supports editing for clarity and fluency.
identified_tools.use_case: The review identifies QuillBot in three studies (El-Garawany, 2023/2024; Marzuki et al., 2023; Thangthong et al., 2024). It is discussed as a paraphrasing and vocabulary-support tool used to assist rephrasing, vocabulary expansion, and writing revision in ESL/EFL writing.

findings.finding_summary: The review reports that QuillBot improved writing performance and self-efficacy by helping learners rephrase text and revise their writing.
The review states that QuillBot broadened learners' vocabulary by suggesting sophisticated synonyms and phrases, supporting vocabulary and style development.

identified_tools.name: Gemini
identified_tools.description: A generative AI assistant used to provide writing support and formative feedback.
identified_tools.use_case: The review names Gemini as one of the notable AI tools and says it appeared in two studies (Thi Thanh, 2025; Waziana et al., 2024). It is discussed as providing formative assessment feedback aligned with professional rubrics and contributing to vocabulary and grammar support.

findings.finding_summary: The review reports that Gemini was noted for consistency in providing formative assessment feedback aligned with professional rubrics.

identified_tools.name: Cami
identified_tools.description: An AI-supported writing tool/platform used in EFL writing instruction, described as integrating multiple AI capabilities for drafting, collaboration, and assessment-related support.
identified_tools.use_case: The review cites Cami as an emerging tool discussed in Muslimin et al. (2024). It says Cami integrates multiple AI technologies to facilitate higher-order tasks such as brainstorming, collaborative writing, and automated grading of paragraph drafts.

findings.finding_summary: The review describes Cami as supporting higher-order writing tasks including brainstorming, collaborative writing, and automated grading of paragraph drafts, indicating positive support for writing development and revision.

identified_tools.name: You.com
identified_tools.description: An AI assistant/search and writing-support platform used for generating and evaluating writing-related outputs.
identified_tools.use_case: The review cites You.com in Özdere (2025) as an emerging AI tool used alongside ChatGPT in academic writing contexts. It is discussed as integrating multiple AI technologies and helping with higher-order tasks such as brainstorming, collaborative writing, and automated grading of paragraph drafts.

findings.finding_summary: The review includes You.com among niche tools found to contribute positively to linguistic improvement and to support higher-order writing tasks.

identified_tools.name: Whisper
identified_tools.description: A speech recognition model/tool mentioned in the review as one of the AI technologies integrated into broader writing-support platforms.
identified_tools.use_case: The review does not discuss Whisper as a standalone intervention. It only mentions that tools like Cami and You.com integrate technologies including Whisper to support writing-related tasks.

identified_tools.name: Stable Diffusion
identified_tools.description: A generative AI model for image generation, mentioned in the review as part of the technology stack integrated into broader AI writing-support platforms.
identified_tools.use_case: The review does not discuss Stable Diffusion as a standalone writing intervention. It is only mentioned as one of the technologies integrated into platforms such as Cami and You.com for higher-order tasks like brainstorming and collaborative work.

identified_tools.name: Perplexity
identified_tools.description: An AI answer-generation/search assistant used to support writing and language tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: The review lists Perplexity as one of the niche AI platforms explored in a smaller subset of included studies. It says these tools contributed positively to linguistic improvement.

findings.finding_summary: The review reports that Perplexity, as part of a smaller subset of niche platforms, contributed positively to linguistic improvement.
findings.measure: Narrative synthesis across cited niche-tool studies

identified_tools.name: Bing Chat
identified_tools.description: A conversational AI assistant integrated with search, used for generating and refining text.
identified_tools.use_case: The review lists Bing Chat among the niche platforms explored in the included literature and says such tools contributed positively to linguistic improvement in ESL/EFL writing contexts.

findings.finding_summary: The review reports that Bing Chat, among other niche tools, contributed positively to linguistic improvement.
findings.measure: Narrative synthesis across cited niche-tool studies

identified_tools.name: Ernie
identified_tools.description: A large language model/chat assistant mentioned as a named AI tool used in writing-related contexts.
identified_tools.use_case: The review lists Ernie among the niche AI platforms discussed in the included studies and says these tools were found to contribute positively to linguistic improvement.

findings.finding_summary: The review reports that Ernie, as one of the niche platforms identified, contributed positively to linguistic improvement.
findings.measure: Narrative synthesis across cited niche-tool studies

identified_tools.name: ProWritingAid
identified_tools.description: An AI writing assistant and editing tool that provides feedback on grammar, style, and writing quality.
identified_tools.use_case: The review includes ProWritingAid in the smaller subset of niche writing platforms and states that such tools contributed positively to linguistic improvement.

findings.finding_summary: The review reports that ProWritingAid, among other niche platforms, contributed positively to linguistic improvement in writing-related outcomes.
findings.measure: Narrative synthesis across cited niche-tool studies

identified_tools.name: DeepL
identified_tools.description: An AI language tool widely used for translation and language support.
identified_tools.use_case: The review mentions DeepL in the literature review section as an example of a more advanced large language model/AI tool alongside ChatGPT and AWE tools like QuillBot and Grammarly. It is mentioned as part of the broader AI landscape supporting writing, but not discussed as a studied intervention in the 31-study synthesis.

identified_tools.name: GPT-4
identified_tools.description: A later-generation version of the GPT-based ChatGPT model, described as more accurate and better at complex tasks than earlier versions.
identified_tools.use_case: The review mentions GPT-4 in the introduction as the latest iteration of ChatGPT released in 2023, and notes prior research saying it is more accurate than ChatGPT 3.5 and better at complex tasks. It is background context rather than a separately synthesized intervention in the included review studies.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT 3.5
identified_tools.description: An earlier ChatGPT version used as a comparison point against newer GPT-4 models.
identified_tools.use_case: The review mentions ChatGPT 3.5 only in the introduction as the earlier version that GPT-4 outperformed in accuracy and complex-task performance. It is not synthesized as a distinct intervention in the included studies.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed systematic literature review using PRISMA 2020 and synthesizing 31 studies, which supports relatively strong evidence quality. However, it is not a formal meta-analysis with pooled effect sizes, and the included evidence base is heterogeneous and heavily skewed toward tertiary settings, so some credibility concerns remain.
impact_tier_rationale: The review reports generally positive effects of AI tools on writing outcomes, especially feedback/revision and grammar, but does not provide a pooled quantitative effect size. Because the magnitude of impact is synthesized narratively and remains somewhat unclear across diverse studies and contexts, the impact is best rated as modest or unclear.
